en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Dukadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (6) 24.22.
Saraṇaduka, Piṭṭhiduka
Section on Dependent Origination, etc.

(Paṭiccādivāra) Dependent on a state that is not to be abandoned by seeing (*na-saraṇa*) and is not to be abandoned by vision (*na-dassana*), a state that is accompanied by clinging (*saraṇa*) and is to be abandoned by vision arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there is one; ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition there is one.

Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*sāraṇa*) and to be abandoned by the vision of the truths (*nanadassanena pahātabba*), there arises a state that is without-conflict (*araṇa*) and not to be abandoned by the vision of the truths (*nadassanena pahātabba*), by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there is one; under predominance-condition there is one ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition there is one.

Dependent on a state that is without-conflict (*nasaraṇa*) and unsurpassed (*nasauttara*), there arises a state that is without-conflict (*araṇa*) but surpassable (*sauttara*), by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there is one; under predominance-condition there is one ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition there is one.
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, dependence, association, and conjunction are similar to the section on dependence [paṭicca]. 24.22.1.7.
Question Section:
Root and Object.
A state that is neither with conflict (*araṇa*) nor surpassable (*anuttara*) is related to a state that is without conflict but surpassable by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … one.
A state that is neither with conflict nor surpassable is related to a state that is without conflict but surpassable by way of the object condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*) … one. (Abbreviated.
One in the case of root, one in the case of object, one in the case of predominance … pe … one in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*).

The state that is with opposition, without conflict, and without superior is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for the state that is without conflict but has a superior; it is a condition by way of co-nascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*);
it is a condition by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*); it is a condition by way of postnascence-condition (*pacchājātapaccaya*) ... (Abbreviated.)
One by way of not-root; one by way of not-object …pe… one by way of not-non-disappearance.
By way of root-condition, one by way of not-object. (Abbreviated.
By way of not-root-condition, one by way of object. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so it should be expanded in detail.
24.22.2. The Supreme State:
Root and Proximity Conditions.

Conditioned by a state that is neither with-conflict (*saraṇa*) nor unsurpassed (*anuttara*), a state that is without-conflict (*araṇa*) and unsurpassed arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. [There is] one under root; ... pe ... one under non-disappearance (*avigata*).
A state that is neither with-conflict nor unsurpassed is a condition, by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*), for a state that is without-conflict and unsurpassed.
(Abbreviated. There is one under proximity, one under contiguity (*samanantara*), one under dependence (*nissaya*), two under decisive support (*upanissaya*), and one under prenascence (*purejāta*).
One [condition] in repetition, one in dissociation, one in presence, one in absence, one in disappearance, and one in non-disappearance.
Exclusion of the Negative (Paccanīyuddhāra):

A state that is not free from conflict (*araṇa*) and not unsurpassed (*anuttara*) is related to a state that is free from conflict and unsurpassed by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*) ... and by way of prenascence condition (*purejāta-paccaya*).
A state with conflict (*sāraṇa*) is related to a state without conflict (*araṇa*) and unsurpassed (*anuttara*) by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

(Abbreviated. There are two [types of relations] under the "not-root" condition, two under the "not-object" condition …pe… one under the "not-decisive-support" condition, two under the "not-prenascence" condition …pe… two under the "not-non-disappearance" condition.
Under the decisive-support condition, there are two [types of relations] under the "not-root" condition. (Abbreviated.)
With non-root condition as the basis for decisive support, there are two; with pre-existence, one ... pe ... with presence, one ... pe ... with non-disappearance, one. (Abbreviated.
(The section on questions should be expanded in the same manner as in the *Kusala-ttika*.
From the beginning of the *Anuloma-dukatika-paṭṭhāna* until the conclusion, the *Paṭṭhāna* consists of thirty recitation sections (*bhāṇavāra*).
The *Duka-Duka-Paṭṭhāna* of the Negative-Conformity (*Paccanīyānuloma*) is completed.
The *Paccanīyānuloma-Paṭṭhāna* is completed.
The *Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa* is completed.
